member.name: P:WizardWrx.HTTP.RequestEngine.Options
member.summary: This immutable reference to a RequestOptions object is a concise way to attach options such as an OAuth access token and a method to get a new token, along with a robust exception logging object that has many configurable settings that determine how much detail it reports and how its reports are delivered.

member.name: M:WizardWrx.HTTP.RequestEngine.#ctor
member.summary: The default constructor leaves the Options property null, which is OK for most use cases.

member.name: M:WizardWrx.HTTP.RequestEngine.#ctor(WizardWrx.HTTP.RequestOptions)
member.summary: This constructor initializes the Options property, which is not strictly required for most use cases, and can be passed in as a RequestOptions constructor call, since the RequestOptions object is a POCO that doesn't even need System; its only reference is to the WizardWrx.DLLConfigurationManager namespace, where the ExceptionLogger lives.
member.param: When supplied, the RequestOptions object reference is stored in the Options property, providing a read-only reference to everything but the OAuth Access Token, which must, of course, be updateable because access tokens are short-lived.

member.name: M:WizardWrx.HTTP.RequestEngine.CallWebApiAndProcessResultASync(System.String,System.Action{Newtonsoft.Json.Linq.JObject},WizardWrx.JsonSupport.JSON_Deserialized_Object,WizardWrx.HTTP.RequestEngine.HttpVerb,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Calls the protected web API and processes the result
member.param: URL of the web API to call (supposed to return Json)

param.name: pfunProcessResultCallback
param.para: This optional Action JObject reference points to the callback used to process the result of the call to the web API. This was intended for processing JSON objects of assorted arbitrary shapes returned by various Microsoft Graph endpoints.
Now that the routine is evolving to meet additional needs, it seemed wiser to abandon the void return type in favor of returning the result in a more conventional fashion.
Though it now returns in a more "natural" way, the callback remains relevant for the Graph API because it allows a single entry point to process

param.name: pjSON_Deserialized
param.para: When present, the optional JSON_Deserialized_Object object is syntactic sugar sprinkled over a standard string that is expected to have passed a very cursory validity check.
This string is the payload required of all POST nad PUT requests.
When this value is null, unless happens to be DELETE, the verb is coerced to GET, the only other verb that dispenses with a payload.

param.name: penmVerb
param.para: This optional member of the HttpVerb enumeration identifies the HTT verb to emit for the request. For backwards compatibility, its value defaults to POST.
When is null, unless this value is DELETE, the verb is coerced to GET, the only other verb that can function without a payload.

member.param: By default, we expect the returned string to be JSON, and use the JsonConvert.DeserializeObject method to return it as a JObject. Otherwise, the raw string is returned as is.

returns.para: This routine was originally intended for use as part of a library that interacts with the Microsoft Graph API and expects to return an arbitrarily shaped object as a JObject, which it passed to the callback routine .

Since it is being pulled out of that class library so that it can be applied elsewhere, it is changed so that it returns whichever object it has, either JSON or an ordinary string. Hence, altough the return type is specified as object, in practice, it is either a JObject or a garden variety String.

member.exception:
Two distinct circumstances can give rise to an Exception exception.
The OAuth token expired and a replacement cannot be obtained from the Microsoft Azure identity server.
Another type of exception arose while processing a request against the Microsoft Graph API endpoints.

An InvalidEnumArgumentException Exception arises when the value of optional argument is invalid, ordinarily due to a programming error, since it is reasonbly safe to assume that the verb is always hard coded per toe API.

member.summary: Instance method CallWebApiAndProcessResultASyn invokes this routine on each iteration of its retry loop to attach HTTP headers directly to the HttpRequestMessage specified by so that the request always provides its own set of request headers.
member.param: This HttpRequestMessage parameter is a reference to the new Request object that is created on each iteration of the request retry loop.

When its value is True, the MediaTypeWithQualityHeaderValue header that represents the JSON MIME type is appended to the headers.

member.name: T:WizardWrx.HTTP.RequestOptions
member.summary: Instances of this object represent options for configuring request behavior, including provision of exception logging tooling and OAuth token retrieval methods.

member.name: T:WizardWrx.HTTP.RequestOptions.OAuthTokenGetter
member.summary: This delegate signature represents a method that attempts to obtain an OAuth token and return it through an output parameter, along with the existing true/false outcome.
member.param: When this method returns, contains the retrieved OAuth token if successful; otherwise, null.
This represents the optional logger object for recording exceptions that arise during token retrieval.
member.returns: The delegated function returns true if the token was successfully obtained; otherwise, it returns false and the value is undefined. The supplied copy of the access token is for use by the HTTP access method; the object that exposes the OAuth Access Token Getter is responsible for stashing a copy in protectd storage.

member.summary: The public constructor initializes both read-only properties of this class, so that consumers of this class must make their choices about these properties explicit.
member.param: The ExceptionLogger instance to be used for logging Exceptions is optional; if no object is supplied, no Exception logging happens inside the other methods exposed by this library.
The delegate that retrieves OAuth Bearer tokens for inclusion in the Authorization header of HTTP requests is optional; if no delegate is provided, requests proceed without Authorization headers.

This optional parameter allows the caller to supply an initial OAuth token that the class caches for future use. If this parameter is null and is not null, the class attempts to obtain a token the first time the property value is queried.
